parts.answer: The ions become free to move throughout the solution, but the water molecules around each ion become ordered (hydration), so the net change is an increase in disorder.
parts.working: 1 mark for free ions; 1 mark for the net change.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Ammonium chloride decomposes: NH₄Cl(s) → NH₃(g) + HCl(g). ΔfH° (kJ mol⁻¹): NH₄Cl(s) −314.4; NH₃(g) −46.1; HCl(g) −92.3. S° (J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹): NH₄Cl(s) 94.6; NH₃(g) 192.3; HCl(g) 186.9. Calculate ΔH° and ΔS°.
parts.answer: ΔH° = +176.0 kJ mol⁻¹; ΔS° = +284.6 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate ΔG° at 298 K and the minimum temperature, in K, at which decomposition is feasible.
parts.answer: ΔG° = +91.2 kJ mol⁻¹ at 298 K (not feasible); T = 618 K
parts.working: 1 mark for ΔG° = 176.0 − 298 × 0.2846 = +91.2 kJ mol⁻¹; 1 mark for T = ΔH°/ΔS° = 618 K; 1 mark for stating feasible above 618 K.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Ammonium nitrate dissolves in water, an endothermic process. Explain the sign of ΔS_surr, and state whether the dissolving is feasible when ΔS_system is positive.
parts.answer: ΔS_surr is negative because the surroundings lose heat (ΔH_sys is positive) so the surroundings lose disorder. Dissolving is feasible when ΔS_sys (positive, from ions freely dispersed) is large enough to make ΔS_total positive, with ΔG negative.
parts.working: 1 mark for ΔS_surr negative; 1 mark for ΔS_sys positive; 1 mark for feasibility from total entropy/ΔG.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the criterion for feasibility in terms of ΔS_total.
parts.answer: ΔS_total = ΔS_sys + ΔS_surr must be positive for a process to be spontaneous.
parts.working: Second law of thermodynamics.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Methane burns: CH₄(g) + 2O₂(g) → CO₂(g) + 2H₂O(g). ΔH° = −802.3 kJ mol⁻¹ at 298 K. S° (J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹): CH₄ 186.3; O₂ 205.2; CO₂ 213.8; H₂O(g) 188.8. Calculate ΔS_system and ΔS_surroundings at 298 K.
parts.answer: ΔS_system = −5.3 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹; ΔS_surr = +2692 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹
parts.working: 1 mark for ΔS_sys = 213.8 + 2(188.8) − (186.3 + 2(205.2)) = −5.3; 1 mark for ΔS_surr = 802 300/298 = 2692 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹; 1 mark for ΔS_total = +2687 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why the reaction is feasible despite ΔS_system being slightly negative.
parts.answer: The total entropy change is +2687 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹, dominated by the large positive ΔS_surr from the heat released, so the reaction is spontaneous.
parts.working: 1 mark for total entropy positive; 1 mark for ΔS_surr dominating.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
State the sign of ΔS_system for each change and give a reason:
(i) sugar dissolves in water
(ii) water vapour condenses to liquid water at 298 K
(iii) a salt crystallises from a saturated solution
parts.answer: (i) positive; (ii) negative; (iii) negative
parts.working: 1 mark each with a reason: (i) solid to ions freely moving; (ii) gas to liquid, fewer molecules free; (iii) ions become ordered in a lattice.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Water is formed as vapour: 2H₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2H₂O(g). Use S° values: H₂ 130.7, O₂ 205.2, H₂O(g) 188.8 (J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹). Calculate ΔS° and state its sign.
parts.answer: ΔS° = -89.0 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹ (negative)
parts.working: 1 mark for 2(188.8) − (2 × 130.7 + 205.2) = −89.0; 1 mark for negative, as 3 gas moles give 2.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Predict how ΔS° would change if liquid water were formed instead, and explain.
parts.answer: It would be more negative (about −327 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹), because the liquid has much lower entropy than the vapour, so more order is created.
parts.working: Gas-to-liquid gives a large decrease.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Use N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) → 2NH₃(g): ΔH° = −92.2 kJ mol⁻¹ and ΔS_sys = −199.1 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹. Calculate ΔS_surr and ΔS_total at 350 K, in J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹ to 3 significant figures.
parts.answer: ΔS_surr = +263 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹; ΔS_total = +64.3 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹
parts.working: 1 mark for ΔS_surr = −ΔH/T = 92 200/350 = 263 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹; 1 mark for ΔS_total = 263 − 199 = +64.3; 1 mark for the sign and conclusion.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State whether the reaction is spontaneous at 350 K.
parts.answer: Yes, because ΔS_total is positive.
parts.working: Second law.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why the entropy of water increases when it boils at 373 K.
parts.answer: Molecules in the vapour are far apart and move randomly over the whole volume, so the disorder increases greatly on vaporisation.
parts.working: 1 mark for more freedom of movement; 1 mark for spread over larger volume.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Methanol boils at 338 K, with ΔH_vap = +35.2 kJ mol⁻¹. Calculate ΔS_vap, in J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹ to 3 significant figures.
parts.answer: 104 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹
parts.working: ΔS_vap = 35 200/338 = 104 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Trouton's rule suggests ΔS_vap is about 88 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹ for many liquids. Suggest why methanol's value is higher.
parts.answer: Methanol is hydrogen bonded in the liquid, which is more ordered than typical liquids; vaporisation releases more disorder than expected.
parts.working: 1 mark for hydrogen bonding; 1 mark for more order in the liquid.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Hydrogen peroxide decomposes: 2H₂O₂(l) → 2H₂O(l) + O₂(g). S° (J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹): H₂O₂(l) 109.6; H₂O(l) 69.9; O₂(g) 205.2. Calculate ΔS° and state its sign.
parts.answer: ΔS° = +125.8 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹ (positive)
parts.working: 1 mark for 2(69.9) + 205.2 − 2(109.6) = +125.8; 1 mark for positive because a gas is formed.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Ammonium nitrate decomposes: NH₄NO₃(s) → N₂O(g) + 2H₂O(g). ΔfH° (kJ mol⁻¹): NH₄NO₃(s) −365.6; N₂O(g) +82.1; H₂O(g) −241.8. S° (J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹): NH₄NO₃(s) 151.1; N₂O(g) 220.0; H₂O(g) 188.8. Calculate ΔH°, ΔS° and ΔG° at 298 K.
parts.answer: ΔH° = -35.9 kJ mol⁻¹; ΔS° = +446.5 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹; ΔG° = -169.0 kJ mol⁻¹
parts.working: 1 mark for ΔH°; 1 mark for ΔS° = 446.5; 1 mark for ΔG° = −35.9 − 298 × 0.4465 = −169.0 kJ mol⁻¹.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why this decomposition is feasible at all temperatures, and why it is explosive in practice.
parts.answer: ΔH° is negative and ΔS° is positive, so ΔG° = ΔH° − TΔS° is negative at every temperature; the reaction is feasible at all T. It is explosive in practice because a large volume of gas and heat is produced very rapidly once started.
parts.working: 1 mark for ΔG° negative from both terms; 1 mark for the large gas formation and exothermic reaction causing explosion.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain, in terms of the sign of ΔS_total, why ΔG° < 0 corresponds to a feasible process, and why ΔG° = 0 at equilibrium.
parts.answer: ΔG° = −TΔS_total (at constant T and P). ΔS_total > 0 gives ΔG° < 0, so the process is feasible. At equilibrium, ΔS_total = 0 and ΔG° = 0.
parts.working: 1 mark for ΔG = −TΔS_total relation; 1 mark for positive ΔS_total giving negative ΔG; 1 mark for zero at equilibrium.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Melting of ice occurs at 273 K with ΔH_fus = +6.01 kJ mol⁻¹. Show that the total entropy change is zero for melting at this temperature, and explain what this means.
parts.answer: ΔS_sys = 6010/273 = +22.0 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹; ΔS_surr = −6010/273 = −22.0 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹; ΔS_total = 0. This means the ice and water are in equilibrium at 273 K.
parts.working: 1 mark for the two equal and opposite entropy changes; 1 mark for equilibrium meaning.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Nitrogen dioxide dimerises: 2NO₂(g) → N₂O₄(g). S° (J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹): NO₂(g) 240.1; N₂O₄(g) 304.4. Calculate ΔS°, and state why the entropy decreases.
parts.answer: ΔS° = -175.8 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹
parts.working: 1 mark for 304.4 − 2(240.1) = −175.8 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹; 1 mark for 2 gas moles giving 1, fewer molecules.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Predict, without calculation, the order of increasing ΔS°: (A) C(s) + O₂(g) → CO₂(g); (B) 2NO(g) + O₂(g) → 2NO₂(g); (C) CaCO₃(s) → CaO(s) + CO₂(g). Explain each position.
parts.answer: Order (lowest first): B < A < C. B has 3 gas moles going to 2 (negative); A has 1 gas mole going to 1 (near zero); C forms a gas from a solid (large positive).
parts.working: 1 mark for C as largest positive (solid to gas); 1 mark for A near zero; 1 mark for B negative with fewer gas moles.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why the entropy change for sublimation of iodine, I₂(s) → I₂(g), is larger than for melting of iodine, I₂(s) → I₂(l).
parts.answer: Sublimation converts a solid directly into a gas, which has far more freedom of movement than a liquid; melting gives only a small increase in disorder, so ΔS(sublimation) > ΔS(melting).
parts.working: 1 mark for gas more disordered than liquid; 1 mark for melting only a small change.
